'''Tejikarao Shrine''' (てぢからおじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Gifu City, Gifu Prefecture.

It is regarded as the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} Hinasumori Shrine of Atsumi District, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}}, though there is also the view identifying {{ill|Hinamori Shrine|Q11547446|qid=Q11547446}} in the same city.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it was enshrined in Jōgan 2 ({{ill|860|Q24714|qid=Q24714}})<ref name="gifu">{{Cite web|ja|title=Gifu City Plan for Maintaining and Improving Historical Scenic Character|publisher=Gifu City|url=https://www.city.gifu.lg.jp/_res/projects/default_project/_page_/001/005/568/keikaku2r40331_s.pdf|accessdate=2023-02-04|page=76}}</ref>.

In {{ill|1600|Q6720|qid=Q6720}} ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 5), during the {{ill|Battle of Sekigahara|Q234188|qid=Q234188}} (prelude: {{ill|Battle of Komeno|Q11604415|qid=Q11604415}}), fighting in the area burned most of the precincts<ref name="gifu"/>.

Main sanctuary rebuilt in {{ill|1616|Q6788|qid=Q6788}} (Genna 2), heiden in 1620, and heiden/worship hall in 1623. Later rebuilt again in Meiji era. In early Meiji, anti-Buddhist measures led to disposal of Buddhist images and implements.

In {{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}} it became {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gōsha}}. On Oct. 18, {{ill|1952|Q5272|qid=Q5272}}, designated {{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}} by Gifu Prefecture Shrine Office.

=== Precincts and surroundings ===
* Main sanctuary / heiden / worship hall
* Shrine office
* First torii
* Second torii (stone)
* Third torii (vermilion)

=== Main rites ===
Spring grand festival is famous as a “fire festival” where men carry a mikoshi loaded with gunpowder and fireworks through the precincts while showered with sparks. It has over 300 years of history and is designated Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Gifu Prefecture<ref name="gifuken bunkazai">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/mumin/gifusi/tejikarahimaturi.html |title=Tejikarao Shrine Fire Festival |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-20}}</ref>.

=== Major annual events ===
; Grand festivals
* Feb 22: Kinen-sai, Kayuzue rite
* 2nd Saturday of April: Spring grand festival ({{ill|Tejikara Fire Festival|Q11496921|qid=Q11496921}})
* Oct 22: Autumn grand festival
* Nov 22: Niiname-sai
; Middle festivals
* Jan 1: Saitan-sai
* Jan 3: Genshi-sai
* Feb 11: Kigensetsu-sai
* Feb 23: Tenchōsetsu-sai
* Dec 9: Chikyūsetsu-sai
; Minor festivals
* Jul 14: Summer festival
* 2nd Saturday of Oct: Memorial rite for war monument
* Nov 15: Shichi-go-san
* Dec 31: New Year’s Eve festival
* 1st and 15th monthly: Tsukinami-sai

=== Cultural properties ===
; Gifu Prefecture designated
* Tejikarao Shrine Fire Festival (Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)

; Gifu City designated
* Wooden monk-form deity statue (sculpture)
* Sacred sake jar (craft)

=== Access ===
* About 5 min south on foot from {{ill|Tejikara Station|id|Stasiun Tejikara|ja|手力駅|jv|Setatsiyun Tejikara|ko|데지카라역|zh|手力站|qid=Q7695230}} (Meitetsu Kakamigahara Line)
